title: Stock counts
description: Count a warehouse and correct its stock.

help.title: About Stock counts
help.overview: A stock count records what is actually on the shelf in one warehouse, then corrects on hand to match. It stays a draft while you count; applying it is the moment the numbers change.

sections.title: The draft
items: A count is for one warehouse, and stays a count of that warehouse.
Each line is a product, an optional variant, the quantity expected when the line was added, and the quantity counted. Lines must be different, stock-tracked items; a bundle cannot be a line.
Leave the counted quantity blank for an item you did not count; apply leaves it alone.
Only a draft can be edited, applied, or cancelled.

sections.title: What apply does
sections.body: The difference is taken against on hand at apply time, not against the expected snapshot.
items: For every counted line, on hand becomes the counted quantity. Sales that shipped while you counted are therefore not undone.
An item the warehouse never stocked gets a new inventory row.
Each change writes an adjustment movement pointing at this count. Applied at and applied by are recorded.
A count below what is reserved for orders is accepted: the shelf is what it is, and available shows the shortfall as negative.
Applying or cancelling needs permission to write the count status.

sections.title: After it is applied
sections.body: The count stays as the record of what was found.
items: Cancel is only from draft. An applied count is not reversed here; count again instead.
An applied count cannot be deleted. A draft or cancelled one is a soft delete and can be restored.
See Inventory for the new on hand and Stock movements for the adjustments.
